purpose: Models communication-delayed scientific dissemination, regional active practice, archive continuity, isolation, political fracture, and reintegration without creating a complete research-graph copy per colony or region.

core_distinctions.scientific_truth: Research-node maturity/resolution describes what has been established by a scientific community; it is not a physical object that teleports everywhere.
core_distinctions.codified_access: Whether a research context currently possesses usable records/data/protocols for known knowledge.
core_distinctions.active_practice: Whether the context has current competence, experts, facilities, tooling, and training sufficient to use/extend knowledge efficiently.
core_distinctions.physical_deployment: Whether actual infrastructure/populations/devices exist; remains owned by the relevant gameplay subsystem.
core_distinctions.rule: A civilization may know a technology historically while an isolated region lacks local records or practical ability to apply it.

research_context.meaning: A scientifically distinct communication/institution context created only when local research access or practice materially diverges from the civilization default.
examples: federation member with autonomous scientific institutions
new successor state after political fracture
research_context.creation_rule: Do not create an explicit context for a normal colony that has the same scientific access/practice as its parent civilization. Create or retain one only when communication isolation, institutional autonomy, censorship, major practice specialization, or polity separation produces meaningful persistent divergence.
research_context.merge_rule: When two contexts have restored communication and their sparse access/practice deviations fall below meaningful thresholds for long enough, merge them back to shared/default state while preserving compressed history.

forbidden_full_copies: complete civilization node-state map when identical to parent/default
complete field competence map when identical to parent/default

knowledge_access_states.meaning: Context has no usable local record of the knowledge beyond possible rumor/history.
Context has summaries or incomplete references sufficient to know the knowledge exists but not to reproduce serious work.
Context has adequate formal records/data/protocols to understand and reconstruct research with suitable facilities/competence.
Context has codified access plus active institutions/expertise maintaining real experimental/engineering practice.

knowledge_dissemination.trigger: A research node state/resolution or strategically meaningful codified asset changes in one context and another authorized context does not already possess equivalent access.
transport_inputs_owned_elsewhere: physical travel time for non-data assets
rules: Ordinary publications/models can propagate after communication latency rather than after physical travel.
Large experimental datasets may be delayed by real bandwidth limits when the communications subsystem reports them as material.
Expert cohorts, prototypes, manufacturing tooling, operating institutions, and other physical/tacit assets do not teleport as data.
Remote training can help only when latency/bandwidth/interface permit it; difficult hands-on practice may still require local experts or physical travel.
Receiving codified knowledge never creates missing facilities, tooling, populations, materials, or engineering practice.
No universal distance research penalty is applied; only actual information/practice constraints matter.

civilization_default_and_exceptions.default_access: Well-connected contexts inherit the civilization's current synchronized codified-access baseline without separate node rows.
civilization_default_and_exceptions.exception_storage: Store only missing/delayed/restricted/locally-advanced node access and locally divergent field practice.
civilization_default_and_exceptions.frontier_advanced_rule: A regional context may temporarily know a discovery before the civilization default synchronizes; store that source context plus pending dissemination rather than pretending every region already knows it.
civilization_default_and_exceptions.default_update_rule: Once all materially connected default contexts have received equivalent codified knowledge, the civilization synchronized baseline can advance and redundant context exceptions are deleted.

field_practice.regional_representation: Sparse deltas/bands only for fields whose local theoretical/experimental/engineering practice materially differs from the synchronized civilization baseline.
field_practice.atrophy_rule: Isolation does not automatically reduce competence; practice declines only when local institutions/training/activity disappear according to the existing competence atrophy model.
field_practice.recovery_rule: Reconnected records can restore theoretical access quickly, but experimental/engineering practice recovers only through actual facilities/training/experts/work.

rules: Destroying one archive does not erase knowledge if independent codified copies survive elsewhere.
A context isolated from surviving copies may lose local codified access after genuine archive destruction/corruption.
Historical awareness that a technology once existed can survive as reference_only even when actionable records are gone.
Recovered external or archaeological records can restore codified access but not automatically active practice.
Censorship can make records inaccessible without physically deleting every copy; later political change can restore access if archives survived.

isolation_causes: extreme communications latency relative to decision/research timescale
reconnection_pipeline: compare context knowledge revisions and archive integrity
exchange newly available codified records according to rights/security/path
resolve conflicting scientific records by provenance/evidence rather than choosing owner by rank
update tacit/training/facility availability only if physical people/assets actually move or institutions cooperate
merge redundant sparse context state when material differences disappear

political_fracture_and_successors.event_owner: governance/politics system decides that polity ownership/fracture occurred; Adaptive Research computes research inheritance from factual local state.
inheritance_rules: A successor does not automatically receive every technology ever known by the former empire.
A successor keeps codified knowledge actually present in inherited contexts/archives even if active practice is weak.
Tacit expertise/facilities follow their real location, people, control, and loyalty—not a global technology checkbox.
Shared foundational knowledge will normally overlap heavily because records are widely replicated; frontier/recent/specialist knowledge can diverge sharply.
Active projects may split, pause, continue locally, or lose necessary participating institutions.
Later diplomacy/trade/reintegration can restore missing knowledge through the normal record/expert/facility pathways.

federation_and_allied_science.rule: Political alliance does not create one merged technology tree.
federation_and_allied_science.rights_and_security: Use the existing technology-exchange/legal-rights model; sharing can be partial, delayed, restricted, revoked, or violated where technically possible.
federation_and_allied_science.joint_project_rule: Participants can contribute real lab/facility/expert capacity only when project coordination and access agreements permit; do not mint free RP because a treaty exists.

cross_workstream_ownership.adaptive_research: knowledge access/practice semantics, context exceptions, dissemination records, research inheritance calculation
cross_workstream_ownership.communications_logistics: communication path, latency, bandwidth, physical travel time, jamming/blockade state
cross_workstream_ownership.governance_politics: polity boundaries, censorship policy, secession/fracture/reintegration decisions
cross_workstream_ownership.construction_economy: physical archive/facility/tooling existence, damage, repair, upkeep
